name: Tennessee

agency.name: Tennessee Bureau of Workers' Compensation (Department of Labor and Workforce Development)

ttd.rateText: Two-thirds (66.67%) of the average weekly wage, computed from gross earnings (including overtime and bonuses) in the 52 weeks before the injury divided by 52; maximum for temporary benefits = 110% of the state average weekly wage (Tenn. Code Ann. § 50-6-207; Bureau rate table).
ttd.minText: Minimum weekly rate as listed in the Bureau rate table ('Mini Rate').
ttd.periodLabel: injuries from July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026 (SAWW $1,297); the July 1, 2026 - June 30, 2027 figures could not be retrieved

waiting.text: TTD benefits start on the eighth day of disability; if the disability lasts 14 days, benefits are back-paid to the first day (Tenn. Code Ann. § 50-6-205).

ttdDuration.text: TTD continues while the authorized treating physician keeps the worker off work, until maximum medical improvement or a return-to-work event; no separate week cap is stated by the Bureau, but total benefits are limited by the maximum total benefit ($583,650 for 2025-26 injuries = 450 weeks x the permanent maximum).

ppd.text: Permanent partial disability is paid at 66 2/3% of the AWW, capped at 100% of the state average weekly wage ($1,297.00 for 2025-26 injuries), based on the impairment rating applied to 450 weeks for the body as a whole (Bureau rate table: 'Body as Whole 450 wks'; Tenn. Code Ann. § 50-6-207).

facts.text: Tennessee's maximum for temporary benefits is 110% of the state average weekly wage, higher than the maximum for permanent benefits (100%).
Temporary disability payments must be paid no later than 15 calendar days after notice of injury; late or unpaid benefits may be penalized.
Burial expenses are covered up to $10,000 and medical benefits are unlimited (Bureau rate table).
Temporary partial disability on light duty is 66 2/3% of the difference between the light-duty gross wage and the pre-injury AWW, within the same max/min.
